section_summary.extract_value: This section introduces 'the present study,' which investigated the relationship between women's body image and subjective happiness using data from the YouBeauty.com Body Image Survey (YBIS). The study involved respondents primarily from the United States and proposed a model where age and education influence BMI, which then affects body dissatisfaction and body appreciation, ultimately impacting subjective happiness.
section_summary.evidence_source: In the present study, we examined associations between women's body image and subjective happiness using data from the YouBeauty.com Body Image Survey (YBIS). More specifically, respondents from the West (primarily the United States) completed two measures of body image, namely weight-related body dissatisfaction (actual-ideal weight discrepancy) and body appreciation. We further examined the impact of respondent age and education on the associations between body image and subjective happiness. We proposed a hypothesised model, derived from the above review of the extant literature, in which education and age shape respondent BMI, which in turn affect body dissatisfaction and body appreciation. The latter two variables were predicted to affect subjective happiness in opposite directions (see Fig. 1).
